canonical_title: Large amplitude heading changes for aggressive agility

versions.title_at_revision: Large amplitude heading changes for aggressive agility
versions.text:
Standard: For air vehicles requiring aggressive agility, in forward flight (greater than 45 KGS), heading changes in one second following an abrupt step displacement of the yaw control are at least 8 degrees or 50% of the operational flight envelope sideslip limit, whichever is smaller. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis to assess large amplitude heading changes in forward flight as specified as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Large-Amplitude Heading Changes for Aggressive Agility (Bandwidth) paragraph for each air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. Apply and hold step input for at least one second while holding other controls fixed. Small control movements, however, are allowed to minimize pitch and roll excursions. Conduct in both directions (left and right). Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess large amplitude heading changes in forward flight as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Large-Amplitude Heading Changes for Aggressive Agility (Bandwidth) paragraph for each air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. Apply and hold step input for at least one second while holding other controls fixed. Small control movements, however, are allowed to minimize pitch and roll excursions. Conduct in both directions (left and right). Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess large amplitude heading changes in forward flight as specified as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Large-Amplitude Heading Changes for Aggressive Agility (Bandwidth) paragraph for selected combinations of air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. Apply and hold step input for at least one second while holding other controls fixed, Small control movements, however, are allowed to minimize pitch and roll excursions. Conduct in both directions (left and right).
